key_facts: Scheduling uses asyncio.create_task() — NO external job queue (no APScheduler, Celery, or RQ)
Scheduled tasks are fire-and-forget asyncio Tasks stored ONLY in memory — lost on bot restart
No job registry, no persistence layer for scheduled publications
No cancel/stop mechanism for scheduled publication cascades
The cascade is a simple for-loop with asyncio.sleep() between publishes
Bot state (FSMContext) is cleared immediately when scheduling starts — quizzes exist only in aiogram FSM state
Database has surveys table but it is NOT used for scheduled publications — it stores completed surveys only
No requirements for APScheduler/Celery in pyproject.toml — pure asyncio approach
call_chain: user clicks ⏰ Programar → handle_schedule() [line 1018] → sets state waiting_schedule_interval
user sends interval → handle_schedule_interval() [line 1038] → parse_interval() [line 206] → validates → asyncio.create_task(_run_scheduled_publish()) [line 1083]
blast_radius: bot/handlers/survey.py — all scheduling logic lives here (lines 203-258, 1018-1156)
bot/database/connection.py — surveys table schema (NOT used for scheduling, only for completed surveys)

data.for_supervisor: VERIFIED: The scheduling system is a simple fire-and-forget asyncio task with NO persistence, NO job registry, and NO cancel mechanism. The cascade is a for-loop with asyncio.sleep() between publishes. If the bot restarts, all scheduled publications are lost. There is no way to cancel a running scheduled cascade — the survey_cancel handler only clears FSM state, not the background task. The quizzes exist only in aiogram FSM memory during scheduling.
data.for_successor: To implement cancel/stop for scheduled publications, you would need to: (1) Create a job registry to track active asyncio.Task objects, (2) Store scheduled publication state (quizzes, interval, progress) in a persistent store, (3) Add a cancel handler that retrieves and cancels the active task, (4) Handle asyncio.CancelledError gracefully in _run_scheduled_publish.
